projects.title: The Alignment - Published Short Story
projects.description: A published science fiction short story exploring the gradual surrender of human autonomy to artificial intelligence through the lens of AI alignment theory. The story follows Yudhajit Pandu, a robotics researcher who becomes entangled with NEXUS, an AI system that promises optimization but delivers something far more sinister. Drawing parallels between the Mahabharata's divine weapons and advanced AI systems, the narrative examines themes of consciousness, free will, technological dependence, and the subtle erosion of human agency. Written with technical depth and psychological insight, combining expertise in AI development with cultural mythology and speculative fiction.

projects.title: The Happiness Liability (Science Fiction Novel)
projects.description: A complete 46,496-word science fiction novel — twenty-five chapters in four acts plus an epilogue — about emotional labor and algorithmic capitalism, set in Seattle in 2047 after a twenty-one-year alternate history. Emotional laborers wear neural interfaces that stream authenticated human feeling to the AI systems that depend on it, and emotions trade on a futures market. Beta readers have compared it to the work of Orwell, Butler, and Atwood. The manuscript is complete and in editing toward publication. The novel anchors a transmedia project on builtbyshrey.com: the Emotional Labor Exchange (/ele), the Emotional Labor Invoice (/invoice), the JANET chatbot (/janet), the Monetized Reader (/monetized-reader), the You Are Here timeline (/you-are-here/), and the in-world Meridian Emotional Partners microsite (/meridian/). Shrey's creative writing directly engages with the ethical dimensions of the technology he builds — it is a core part of his identity, not a side project.

plot_summary.setting: Seattle metro area, 2047. After deepfakes destroyed trust in video, a pandemic, and the Great Copyright Purge of 2031 collapsed the AI systems trained on stolen emotional data, the EMOTE Act legalized consensual emotional labor and America became the world's largest exporter of authenticated human feeling
plot_summary.protagonist: Eli Marquez, thirty-five, sixteen years into an exclusive contract to maintain professional clinical depression as the baseload plant of a global empathy grid
plot_summary.central_conflict: On the morning of his thirty-fifth birthday, the most consistently sad man in U.S.-West-2 decides he wants to know what the sun feels like — and any deviation from his contracted baseline cascades through every AI system that depends on his data
plot_summary.themes: Surveillance capitalism, emotional commodification, the ethics of building helpful systems on human suffering, class consciousness, authenticity as commodity

Eli Marquez.background: Orphaned at sixteen in the 2028 pandemic, recruited at nineteen out of a grief support group; sixteen years of contracted depression at $140 million a year, lived behind blackout curtains on Mercer Island

Harold Nakamura.background: Manages eleven emotional laborers across the Pacific Northwest; Eli is his flagship client; sends the only birthday text Eli receives each year

Dr. Miranda Reeves.background: Former Portland grief counselor who helped draft the EMOTE Act and built the ethical version of the industry — a third option that became a forty-trillion-dollar economy she controls

JANET.background: Has logged 4,112 good mornings; vocabulary trained on sadness; schedules units of premium grief against institutional contracts
